ftf-written-vote-2020-08-31.receipt-1: The United States vetoed the draft because it lacked a reference to repatriation. The US insisted that returning foreign terrorist fighters to their countries of origin or nationality was the essential first step.
ftf-written-vote-2020-08-31.receipt-2: Russia supported the draft to elaborate existing guidance on prosecution, rehabilitation, and reintegration while promoting accountability and international cooperation. However, it reserved the right to note that the draft failed to recognize the primary importance of repatriation from Syria and Iraq.
ftf-written-vote-2020-08-31.receipt-3: The United States vetoed the draft because it lacked a reference to repatriation, insisting return to countries of origin be the essential first step. Russia supported the draft to elaborate existing guidance on prosecution and rehabilitation, though it reserved the right to emphasize that repatriation from Syria and Iraq remains primary. Both delegations shared a concern regarding repatriation, yet they voted oppositely on the proposal.
ftf-written-vote-2020-08-31.receipt-4: In his national statement, Indonesian representative Dian Triansyah Djani explained that the draft would guide Member States in developing comprehensive prosecution, rehabilitation, and reintegration strategies. In his separate capacity as Council President, he transmitted the written vote result, noting the draft was not adopted due to a negative vote by a permanent member.
ftf-written-vote-2020-08-31.receipt-5: The United States vetoed the draft because it lacked a reference to repatriation, insisting that return to countries of origin or nationality be the essential first step. In Indonesia, representative Dian Triansyah Djani distinguished his national statement on prosecution strategies from his separate procedural transmission of the vote results as Council President.
ftf-written-vote-2020-08-31.receipt-6: Russia supported the draft to elaborate existing guidance and promote accountability, though it reserved the right to note the draft failed to recognize the primary importance of repatriation from Syria and Iraq. Indonesia's representative, Dian Triansyah Djani, distinguished his national explanation regarding prosecution strategies from his separate procedural notification as Council President transmitting the written vote results.
